timberline-hdz-charcoal.title: GAF Timberline HDZ Charcoal Shingles
timberline-hdz-charcoal.description: Architectural laminate shingles in deep charcoal, featuring LayerLock technology that considerably widens the nailing zone for a faster, surer fastening.
about: Timberline HDZ (GAF) is the best selling GAF shingle, a fiberglass asphalt architectural shingle shown here in Charcoal, one of its High Definition colors. LayerLock Technology powers StrikeZone, the largest nailing zone in the industry, and Dura Grip thermal sealant bonds the shingles together once they are exposed to sun and warm temperatures, so they stay in place under high wind.

Each shingle measures 13 1/4 x 39 3/8 in (337 x 1,000 mm) with a 5 5/8 in (143 mm) exposure. A square takes 64 pieces in 3 bundles. GAF matches it with TimberTex or TimberCrest ridge cap and Pro Start, QuickStart or WeatherBlocker starter strips at eaves and rakes. Install on slopes of 2:12 or greater over a deck of at least 3/8 in (10 mm) plywood or OSB. From 2:12 to under 4:12 the deck takes two layers of GAF Roof Deck Protection; at 4:12 and above, one.

Use zinc coated steel or aluminum roofing nails of 10 to 12 gauge with 3/8 to 7/16 in (10 to 12 mm) heads, long enough to penetrate 3/4 in (19 mm) into the deck, driven flush. The standard pattern is 4 nails about 6 7/8 in (174 mm) from the bottom of the shingle; some codes require 6. Mansard roofs of 21:12 and above are nailed 6 in (152 mm) from the bottom and hand sealed with 4 dabs of shingle tab adhesive.

Warranty: Lifetime coverage against manufacturing defects for the original owner of a single family home, or an eligible second owner. The 15 year WindProven Limited Wind Warranty, with no maximum wind speed, applies to LayerLock shingles installed with the required GAF starter strips, roof deck protection and other qualifying GAF accessories. StainGuard Plus adds a 25 year limited algae warranty using time release algae fighting technology.

brakki-10pc.title: Dark Ribbed Steel Roofing Panels 10 Pack
brakki-10pc.description: Grey ribbed galvanized steel roofing panels supplied as a ten piece package covering approximately seventy five square feet, screws included.
about: Brakki sells these panels as a ready to fit pack rather than as a factory run cut to your roof, so a small building arrives complete in one delivery. The sheets are ribbed galvanized steel in grey, each one measuring 61.02 x 17.72 in (1,550 x 450 mm), and ten come in the box. Grooved side edges interlock, which keeps the seam tight and makes the sheets quicker to line up on a frame. Nothing has to be cut or formed on site at all.

The ten piece pack covers 75.3 sq ft in total, which is the gross sheet area rather than the net area once the sheets overlap, so allow for the side and end laps when you work out how many packs a roof needs. Steel thickness is 0.01 in (0.25 mm). Fifty screws ship in the box, five per sheet, along with a pair of gloves for handling the cut edges safely. Brakki offers the same profile in a ten piece pack when the job is bigger.

Brakki lists the panels for garages, chicken coops, sheds, stables and patio covers, which is the work a light gauge sheet is meant for. They fasten straight through the flat of the profile into timber or steel purlins using the screws supplied. Lay each sheet so it laps the groove of the one before it, work from the eave upward, and keep the laps turned away from the prevailing wind. A cordless driver with a hex socket is the only tool needed.

Galvanizing is what carries the corrosion resistance here, and Brakki rates the finish as UV resistant and colourfast so the grey holds up in full sun. At 0.01 in this is a light gauge sheet built for outbuildings, not a substitute for a structural roof panel on a house. No warranty term, wind rating or fire classification is published for the pack, so treat it as accessory grade. Check local code before putting it over habitable space.

brakki-stone-tiles.title: DECRA Stone Coated Steel Roof Tiles
about: DECRA Tile is a pressure formed steel panel finished with a ceramic coated stone chip surface, so a roof reads as Mediterranean clay tile while weighing a fraction of it. The steel is aluminium zinc alloy coated to ASTM A792 at 26 gauge, 0.0179 in (0.455 mm), and each panel is pre corrugated into several vertical tiles forming one tile step across its face. The colour comes from the stone granules rather than a paint film that could chalk.

Each panel measures 16 1/2 x 52 in (419 x 1,321 mm) and installs to an exposure of 14 1/2 x 50 in (368 x 1,270 mm), which works out at twenty panels to the square. Installed weight is 150 lb per 100 sq ft, roughly a seventh of what concrete tile puts on the same structure, so DECRA Tile is often the option on a reroof where the frame cannot take more load. Matching valley, side and roof to wall flashings are pressed from the same 26 gauge steel.

Minimum slope is 3:12. Between 2:12 and 3:12 the deck takes an additional underlayment layer before the battens go down. The panel is listed for batten installation under ICC-ES report ESR-2901 and Florida approval FL9759-R9. Panels nail through the batten rather than face fixing, so no fastener head is left exposed to weather on the finished roof. Battens may be timber or steel, and counter battens are an option where drainage needs it.

Warranty: lifetime limited on a single family detached home, covering blow off in wind speeds up to 120 mph and hail stone penetration, cracking or splitting up to a 2.5 in stone. The system carries ASTM E108 and UL 790 Class A for fire and UL 2218 Class 4 for impact, which is the top impact class and often earns an insurance discount. Fasteners follow ANSI/ASME B18.6.1 for wood screws and B18.6.4 for thread forming tapping screws.

brakki-insulated-panel.title: Isodomus Insulated Sandwich Panel
about: Isodomus is an insulated sandwich panel from Isopan that arrives as a finished roof in one piece: a pressed steel outer sheet in a barrel tile shape, a rigid polyurethane core and a second steel sheet on the inside. One panel replaces tile, batten and insulation at once, which is why it turns up on rural and public buildings where a tiled look is required but the structure is light. Isopan makes the range in Italy in colours that imitate traditional tile.

The useful covering width is 1,000 mm and the tile pattern repeats on a 350 mm module with a profile height of 50 mm. The outer sheet is 0.5 mm steel and the inner sheet 0.4 mm, with a 0.6 mm aluminium outer face offered as an alternative. Core thicknesses start at 30 mm and rise from there, and working length is held to a tolerance of plus or minus 2 mm under EN 14509. Catalogue weight tables are given separately for steel and mono faced versions.

Fixing is the penetrating type, driven through the panel with exposed caps, and the number and position of the fasteners has to be worked out from the loads on the roof rather than taken as a fixed pattern. Minimum slope is seven percent. Published load tables run from a 1,050 mm span up to 3,500 mm, so the purlin spacing follows the core thickness chosen. Counter battens are not part of the system, so drainage is handled by the panel profile itself.

Thermal transmittance runs from 0.55 W/m2K on the thinnest core down to 0.19 W/m2K on the thickest, calculated to EN ISO 6946 and declared under UNI EN 14509:2007. The panel is light enough to help on seismic loads and fast enough to close a roof in a day, which is where most of its value sits on a refurbishment job. Isopan also lists a Classic version of the same panel with a different tile step running across its visible face.

duration-designer-slatestone-grey.title: Duration Designer Slatestone Grey
duration-designer-slatestone-grey.description: Architectural shingles incorporating a SureNail fabric strip that reinforces the nailing zone against powerful winds on particularly exposed coastal roofs.
about: Duration Designer (Owens Corning) is an architectural shingle from the TruDefinition Duration series, in Slatestone Grey. Its patented SureNail Technology is the only reinforced nailing zone on the face of a shingle: a woven fabric strip embedded across both layers, giving Triple Layer Protection against nail pull and up to 200% wider bond between the layers than standard shingles. Tru Bond weathering grade asphalt sealant holds each course down.

Each shingle is nominally 13 1/4 x 39 3/8 in with a 5 5/8 in exposure. A square takes 64 shingles in 3 bundles, covering 98.4 sq ft. StreakGuard blends copper lined 3M granules into the surface against blue green algae; Owens Corning Hip and Ridge shingles match the Designer colors. The deck can be 6 in boards, 3/8 in plywood or 7/16 in OSB. From 4:12 up, Owens Corning synthetic underlayment or one meeting ASTM D8257; from 2:12 to under 4:12, two layers.

Use galvanized steel, stainless steel or aluminum nails with a minimum 12 gauge shank and 3/8 in head, placed inside the SureNail fastening area and driven at least 3/4 in into the wood deck or through it by 1/4 in, preferably meeting ASTM F1667. Slopes over 60 degrees (21 in per foot) require six nails and four spots of asphalt roofing cement per shingle. Store bundles flat in a covered, ventilated area below 110°F, handling them with care below 40°F.

Warranty: Limited Lifetime. Wind coverage reaches up to 160 mph when the Owens Corning component requirements are met and starter shingles are installed on both the eaves and the rakes. The 25 year algae resistance coverage, effective January 1, 2024, requires an approved Owens Corning Hip and Ridge product. The Class 3 impact rating comes from laboratory testing and does not guarantee all weather resistance; hail damage is excluded.

steeldash-snap-lock-slate-gray.title: Steeldash Slate Gray Standing Seam
about: This is Steeldash snap lock standing seam in 24 gauge steel, finished in Slate Gray. The seam closes by pressing one panel onto the last, so there is no mechanical seaming pass and no crew standing on a seamer for a day. The clips sit under the seam and never show, which is the whole point of a standing seam roof next to an exposed fastener panel. Steeldash rolls the same profile in Galvalume bare and in a run of solid colours besides this one.

Net coverage is 16 in per panel with a major rib height of 1 in, and the pan is flat as standard. Panels are rolled to order from 1 ft up to 40 ft in half foot increments, so a run from eave to ridge usually arrives as a single length with no end lap to seal. Lead time from Steeldash is quoted at seven business days before shipping. A striated pan is available on request, which is the usual answer to oil canning across wide runs of pan.

Steeldash calls for installation over a solid substrate with an underlayment between the panel and the deck, which rules out open purlins for this profile. Minimum recommended roof slope is 3 in 12. Because the clips are concealed and the seam snaps rather than screws, nothing penetrates the water plane across the field of the roof. The underlayment choice is left to the installer, so a high temperature membrane is worth specifying.

Warranty: the paint system is covered for 40 years against peeling and 30 years against chalk or fade. Steel is supplied mill certified. No wind uplift, fire or impact classification is published for the panel on its own, so if a job needs a rated assembly the numbers have to come from Steeldash for the specific build up. The colour itself is a factory applied coating, so no site painting is involved at any stage of the installation.

malarkey-smart-start.title: Malarkey Smart Start Starter Shingles
malarkey-smart-start.description: Perforated NEX polymer modified starter shingle separating into two independent strips that seal the foundational course along eaves and rakes.
about: Smart Start (Malarkey SKU 210) is a NEX polymer modified starter shingle for steep slope residential roofs. It is manufactured on a non woven fiberglass mat, coated on both sides with NEX polymer modified bitumen compounded with a fire retardant mineral stabilizer, and mineral surfaced. Malarkey requires Smart Start, or an equivalent conforming to ASTM D3462, under all of its shingles, including Windsor, and recommends it on the rake edges too.

Each full size shingle measures 16 3/8 x 38 1/4 in (416 x 972 mm). A perforation in the middle, 8 3/16 in (208 mm) from each edge, splits it lengthwise into two code compliant starter pieces of 8 3/16 x 38 1/4 in (208 x 972 mm), each with its own factory applied seal down strip, for exposures up to 6 3/16 in. A bundle holds 18 full size shingles (36 pieces) and covers 114 ft 9 in (35 m); a pallet carries 21 bundles. Typical granule adhesion is 0.3 g.

Lay the starter with the seal down strip at the roof edge, overhanging eave and rake by 1/4 to 3/4 in (6 to 19 mm); on 3 tab and laminate roofs, cut 6 in (152 mm) off the first piece to offset the end joints. Fasten each with four nails 1 1/2 to 3 in (38 to 76 mm) up from the eave, one 1 in (25 mm) from each end and two between them, never through the seal down strip. Slopes over 21 in per 12 in need six nails. Butt pieces loosely to prevent buckling.

Nail heads must be at least 3/8 in (10 mm) and driven flush, not over or under driven or angled; staples are not allowed. Do not use it on slopes under 2:12. Store it cool, dry and well ventilated; do not double stack pallets. Smart Start qualifies for Limited Lifetime Warranty coverage when installed with Malarkey shingles and one other Malarkey accessory; full terms and any extra requirements are in the Malarkey Shingle and Accessory Warranty.

landmark-weathered-wood.title: Landmark Weathered Wood Shingles
landmark-weathered-wood.description: Dual layer laminate shingle cut to a diamond tab, delivering approximately thirty three square feet within every individual bundle supplied.
about: Landmark (CertainTeed) is a laminated architectural shingle, in Weathered Wood. It is built on a fiberglass mat with ceramic coated mineral granules in refined, water resistant asphalt; two pieces are laminated with a tough asphaltic cement, and every shingle carries self sealing adhesive strips and NailTrak. The Algae Resistant (AR) version prevents the dark streaks caused by blue green algae (Gloeocapsa magma); AR is not available in every region.

Each shingle measures 13 1/4 x 38 3/4 in with a 5 5/8 in weather exposure. A square takes 65 shingles in 3 bundles, covers approximately 98.4 sq ft and weighs 211 to 225 lb, depending on the manufacturing plant. Use it on slopes greater than 2 in per foot; low slope applications from 2:12 to under 4:12 need additional underlayment, and where ice can back up at the eaves CertainTeed specifies WinterGuard waterproofing underlayment or an equivalent.

Installation instructions are printed on every bundle. Hips and ridges take Shadow Ridge, Cedar Crest or Mountain Ridge in a matching color. No maintenance is required when installed to CertainTeed instructions, but inspect the roof yearly. In Florida the rake starter can be waived when shingles are set in a 4 in bed of asphalt roofing cement per code. As part of an Integrity Roof System, the roof qualifies for unlimited wind velocity coverage.

Warranty: lifetime limited and transferable against manufacturing defects, with up to 10 years of SureStart protection; AR shingles add a 25 year algae resistance warranty when installed with the CertainTeed hip and ridge caps above. Standard wind coverage is 110 mph for 15 years, upgradeable to 160 mph with CertainTeed hip and ridge caps plus SwiftStart, SwiftStart SA or High Performance Starter at the eaves and rakes; roof overs are not permitted.

dynasty-emerald-green.title: IKO Dynasty Emerald Green Shingles
dynasty-emerald-green.description: Architectural laminate shingles with a reinforced ArmourZone nailing band, rated for powerful winds and protected by a limited lifetime warranty.
about: Dynasty (IKO) is a heavyweight laminated shingle, shown here in Emerald Green, made on a dimensionally stable non woven glass fiber mat impregnated with stabilized waterproofing bitumen. It has a random shake look with high contrast dual band shadow coloring, colored ceramic granules on both layers to protect the asphalt from ultraviolet radiation, release tape and mineral powder on the underside, and algae inhibiting granules for lasting resistance.

Each shingle measures 40 7/8 x 13 3/4 in (1,038 x 349 mm) with a 5 7/8 in (149 mm) exposure and a 2 in (50 mm) headlap. A bundle holds 20 shingles and covers 33.3 sq ft (3.1 m²); a pallet of 40 x 53 in carries 56 bundles. The ArmourZone nailing area is wider for faster installation and is backed by ArmourZone tape on the reverse side for added protection against wind loss, and a thermally activated sealant bonds each course.

Suitable for slopes greater than 4:12, with underlayment strongly recommended below 6:12. Low slopes from 2:12 to 4:12 need two plies of felt or one of IKO Ice and Water Protector. Install it with roofing nails, never staples, exactly as printed on the bundle wrapper, with IKO starter strip shingles at the eaves; rake starters are not required for Dynasty. Cap hips and ridges with an IKO approved shingle such as Marathon Plus AR or IKO UltraHP.

Warranty: Limited Lifetime, with non prorated Iron Clad Protection for the first 180 months (15 years) and prorated coverage after that. For the same 15 years it is covered against wind blow off for gusts up to 130 mph, provided it was nailed as the wrapper instructs and has sealed down or been hand sealed; manual sealing is not required in Florida. The algae resistance warranty runs 120 months (10 years).

brakki-22pc.title: Bare Corrugated Steel Panels 20 Pack
brakki-22pc.description: Bare galvanized corrugated steel roofing panels supplied as a twenty piece package covering approximately one hundred eighty total square feet.
about: This is the same Brakki pack in the classic wavy corrugated profile, left bare rather than painted, so the finish you see is the galvanized coating itself. Each sheet measures 73.23 x 17.72 in (1,860 x 450 mm) and twenty of them come in the box. The rounded corrugations sit closer together than a ribbed profile, which stiffens a thin sheet and hides small dents better once it is up on a frame. Nothing has to be cut or formed on site.

The twenty piece pack covers 180.19 sq ft in total, which is the gross sheet area rather than the net area once the sheets overlap, so allow for the side and end laps when you work out how many packs a roof needs. Steel thickness is 0.01 in (0.25 mm). One hundred screws ship in the box, five per sheet, along with a pair of gloves for handling the cut edges safely. Brakki offers the same profile in a ten piece pack when the job is smaller.

Brakki lists the panels for garages, chicken coops, sheds, stables and patio covers, which is the work a light gauge sheet is meant for. They fasten straight through the flat of a corrugation into timber or steel purlins using the screws supplied. Overlap by a full corrugation at the sides, work from the eave upward, and keep the laps turned away from the prevailing wind. A cordless driver with a hex socket is the only tool needed for the job.

Left bare, the panel weathers to a matt grey rather than staying bright, and there is no paint film to chalk or peel. At 0.01 in this is a light gauge sheet built for outbuildings, not a substitute for a structural roof panel on a house. No warranty term, wind rating or fire classification is published for the pack, so treat it as accessory grade material. Check local code before putting it over any habitable space below the deck.

steeldash-snap-lock-ash-gray.title: Steeldash Ash Gray Striated Panel
about: This is Steeldash snap lock standing seam in 24 gauge steel, finished in Ash Gray. The seam closes by pressing one panel onto the last, so there is no mechanical seaming pass and no crew standing on a seamer for a day. The clips sit under the seam and never show, which is the whole point of a standing seam roof next to an exposed fastener panel. Steeldash rolls the same profile in Galvalume bare and in a run of solid colours besides this one.

Net coverage is 16 in per panel with a major rib height of 1 in, and this one carries the striated pan. Panels are rolled to order from 1 ft up to 40 ft in half foot increments, so a run from eave to ridge usually arrives as a single length with no end lap to seal. Lead time from Steeldash is quoted at seven business days before shipping. The flat pan is the standard option, so the striated version has to be called in when ordering.

Steeldash calls for installation over a solid substrate with an underlayment between the panel and the deck, which rules out open purlins for this profile. Minimum recommended roof slope is 3 in 12. Because the clips are concealed and the seam snaps rather than screws, nothing penetrates the water plane across the field of the roof. The underlayment choice is left to the installer, so a high temperature membrane is worth specifying.

Warranty: the paint system is covered for 40 years against peeling and 30 years against chalk or fade. Steel is supplied mill certified. No wind uplift, fire or impact classification is published for the panel on its own, so if a job needs a rated assembly the numbers have to come from Steeldash for the specific build up. The colour itself is a factory applied coating, so no site painting is involved at any stage of the installation.
